st.headline: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
st.teaser: Unofficially, the Nasdaq gained 1.09% to 24,579.43 points.
fullText: NEW YORK - Technology stocks bounced back on Nov 6 from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite Index posted a fourth consecutive weekly decline as investors sifted for clues about what comes next in the AI trade.
Gains within technology were broadly shared, with the semiconductor index rallying and Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Sandisk rebounding.

The broad revival underscores investor faith in the AI buildout that has driven US stock indexes to dozens of record closes this year, despite a shakeout that began with a US long-term Treasury yield spike in August and the stock volatility of the past month.

“We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market,” said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services in Atlanta. “We are still giving technology the benefit of the doubt.”
Unofficially, the S&P 500 climbed 0.32% to end the session at 7,376.92 points.
The Nasdaq gained 1.09% to 24,579.43 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.46% to 51,286.21 points.

Lerner said he views the selloff this week, which has taken the Nasdaq into correction territory denoting a 10% decline from its peak a month ago, as likely offering a longer-term buying opportunity for many investors.
“AI has gone on trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial in Charlotte, North Carolina.
Referring to the US midterm election results that spurred heavy selling in AI stocks, he said, “This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction.”
The S&P 500 sectors were mixed, with information technology leading gains and consumer staples and healthcare lagging. The benchmark index headed for its worst week since June.
US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting the labour market remained resilient.
Traders added to bets that the Federal Reserve could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78% chance of a December move compared with a 70% chance seen earlier, according to LSEG.

“Those are strong numbers,” said Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. But he asked: “Will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?“
Tesla and SpaceX were among technology shares bouncing back from the Nov 6 plunge.
Among other stock movers, software firm Atlassian dropped after reporting first-quarter results.
Airbnb climbed after the vacation rental platform raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.

Oil prices were slightly lower, adding to bullish sentiment for riskier assets, and were on track for sharp weekly declines. The S&P 500 energy index was on track for a double-digit weekly percentage drop.

Despite the volatility, Turnquist said a bullish sign for the AI buildout is the performance of copper, a major ingredient in data centre buildouts and other technology. Copper futures remain above their 200-day moving average and their September lows, he said.
“If this is real demand destruction on AI, you’d think copper would start to roll over,” Turnquist said. “It’s not a perfect barometer, but I look at it as a reality check.” REUTERS

cna.headline: India's Shami keeps white-ball focus after ending test career
cna.teaser: India's Shami keeps white-ball focus after ending test career
fullText: Nov 7 : India fast bowler Mohammed Shami said he would continue playing white-ball cricket and remain available for domestic multi-day matches after retiring from test cricket on Friday, bringing the curtain down on a 13-year red-ball career.

The 36-year-old, who took 229 wickets in 64 tests after making a memorable debut against West Indies in 2013, announced his decision in a video posted on social media on the anniversary of his first test appearance.
"Let's end this 13-year journey here today," Shami said.
"I made my debut today, and today I am taking retirement. I am leaving this, but I will continue to play white-ball cricket, whether it is IPL or domestic.

His final test appearance came in the World Test Championship final against Australia in 2023, but he continued to play limited-overs cricket before injuries and fitness concerns hampered his appearances for India.

Shami, India's all-time leading wicket-taker in 50-over World Cups with 55 wickets, last featured for India in a one-day international against New Zealand last year and in a Twenty20 match against England in February 2025.
He currently represents Bengal in domestic cricket and plays for Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League.
